data.text/markdown:
Borrowing strength across a graph

A complete regression experiment · CPU · seeded synthetic data · ADMM A stratified model gives each group its own regression coefficients. Graph regularization encourages connected groups to agree. This sits between fitting one model for everybody and fitting every group independently. This experiment makes the trade-off visible: the true coefficient field is known, one group has no training observations, and every method is evaluated on the same independent test snapshot. Explore the graph and its strength, inspect the estimated coefficients, and distinguish predictive accuracy from coefficient smoothing and sparsity.

data.text/html:
The selected graph is defined by the control below. The model and transform recipes are immutable. A fit returns a typed success or failure. 
features = ("x", "noise", "intercept")
recipe = Pipeline(
preprocessing=compose(AddIntercept(name="intercept")),
model=RegressionSpec(
    features=features,
    axes=(selected_graph.axis,),
    penalties=(
        L1(name="sparsity", weight=0, features=("x", "noise")),
        L2(name="shrinkage", weight=0.004, features=features),
        Laplacian(name="smoothing", weight=0.01,
                  graph=selected_graph, features=features),
    ),
),
)
result = fit(recipe, train_x, train_y, solver=ADMM())

The experiment currently shown

Graph weight: 0.01 · L1: 0 · L2: 0.004 · training rows: 168 Group 4 is absent from training. Its stratified coefficients can be informed by neighbors; its independent fit is identified by the local L2 penalty. The irrelevant noise feature has true coefficient zero.

Predictive evidence and solve quality

Compare held-out errors first, then inspect whether the requested optimizations actually converged.
A stronger graph penalty reduces differences between connected coefficients. It can reduce variance in sparse groups, but excessive smoothing introduces bias. A wrong graph may make predictions worse. L1 can remove irrelevant coefficients; that is a different effect from smoothing or improving test error.

{
  "seed": 17,
  "data": "seeded synthetic smooth coefficient field",
  "objective": "global mean squared loss / 2 + local and graph penalties",
  "weights": {
    "graph": 0.01,
    "l1": 0.0,
    "l2": 0.004
  },
